acceptance_criteria.criterion: The Knowledge page renders a tab bar ("Global" / "Repository"); switching tabs immediately filters the card list to the corresponding scope without a round-trip
Global tab renders a filter bar with category dropdown and free-text search; Repository tab adds a project dropdown
Filtering works client-side without a round-trip
Each card displays scope badge, category pill, tags, content preview, confidence percentage with bucket label, source, and timestamps
Inline editing saves changes via API.updateKnowledge and updates the card in-place without a page reload
Delete shows an inline confirmation step before removing the card
Promote to Global moves a project-scoped card to global scope and re-renders in-place
Move to Project accepts a target slug input and re-renders the card with the new scope
formatConfidence renders 80% (High), 50% (Medium), 10% (Low) correctly with bucket thresholds as named constants
No Router._setPolling() call is made — knowledge is not auto-refreshed
Error states are shown via showError(app, ...) when API calls fail

summary: Created mcp-server/gui/public/views/knowledge.js implementing the full renderKnowledge(app) SPA view. Deliverables: tab bar (Global/Repository) with client-side scope filtering; per-tab filter bars (Global: category + search; Repository: project + category + search); formatConfidence() helper with CONFIDENCE_HIGH_MIN=68 and CONFIDENCE_MEDIUM_MIN=34 named constants producing '80% (High)', '50% (Medium)', '10% (Low)'; buildKnowledgeHtml() rendering scope badge, category pill, tag chips, 200-char content preview, confidence label, source, and timestamps; applyFilters() for client-side tab/category/project/query filtering; inline edit form with title, content, category, tags, and range slider with live confidence display; delete inline confirmation (Confirm/Cancel); Promote to Global for project-scoped cards; Move to Project with inline slug input; all API calls use API.updateKnowledge/deleteKnowledge/promoteKnowledge/moveKnowledge; error states via showError(app, ...); no Router._setPolling() call.

comments.note: views/knowledge.js: wireFilterBarEvents() and wireEvents() both contain inline logic to collect distinct categories/projects from allInsights. This duplication could be extracted into a getDistinctValues() helper to reduce drift risk if category/slug collection logic needs updating.

views/knowledge.js: The load() function handles both array responses (Insight[]) and object responses ({ insights: [...] }) defensively. handleListKnowledge returns Insight[] directly, so the data.insights branch will never be hit. The defensive check is harmless but adds minor noise.

views/knowledge.js: renderList() re-creates the filter bar HTML and re-wires its event listeners on every card re-render (triggered by every keystroke in the search input). For small knowledge stores (< 1,000 entries as stated in plan) this is fine, but it could cause input focus loss if the filter bar is rebuilt while the user is typing. The query input loses focus on each keystroke. Consider only rebuilding the card list and keeping the filter bar stable.

views/knowledge.js: The query search input loses focus on each keystroke because renderList() rebuilds the filter bar DOM. A minimal fix would be to cache filterQuery before rebuilding and refocus the input after, or separate card-list re-render from filter-bar re-render (only rebuild filter bar on tab switch).

summary: Full Verification Stack executed against mcp-server/gui/public/views/knowledge.js.
BUILD CHECK: No syntax errors. File is pure ES5-compatible vanilla JS with no imports/requires — loads correctly as a browser script.

AC VERIFICATION: All 11 ACs verified PASS. Tab bar renders 'Global'/'Repository' with correct data-tab attributes. Filter bar structure correct (Global: category+search; Repository: project+category+search). Client-side applyFilters() covers scope, category, project, and free-text (title/content/tags). Card rendering confirmed: scope badge, category pill, tag chips, 200-char content preview, confidence label, source, timestamps. Inline edit form pre-populates all 5 fields from the existing insight object. Delete flow: first click sets confirmDeleteId (shows confirm/cancel), API.deleteKnowledge only called on confirm-delete. Promote and Move handlers both use pre-operation id to filter allInsights before pushing newInsight. formatConfidence: CONFIDENCE_HIGH_MIN=68, CONFIDENCE_MEDIUM_MIN=34 confirmed; 14 boundary cases tested including 0.33→Low, 0.34→Medium, 0.67→Medium, 0.68→High, 0.80→High, 0.10→Low. No Router._setPolling() call — verified by grep (zero occurrences). Error states: 4 of 5 catch blocks use showError(app, ...) — load, delete, promote, move all PASS.
REGRESSION: No other view files modified. knowledge.js is not yet wired into router.js/index.html (WP-008 scope) — no regression risk from this WP.

EDGE-CASE STRESS TESTS: (1) null title/content/tags insight does not crash applyFilters — the guard conditions (ins.title && ..., ins.content && ..., ins.tags && ...) correctly short-circuit. (2) Empty tags array handled by filter(Boolean) in tags parser. (3) Content preview exact-200-char boundary correctly omits ellipsis; 201-char correctly adds ellipsis. (4) Empty targetSlug guard in confirm-move blocks submission. (5) Case-insensitive search (ALPHA matches 'Alpha'). (6) Tab switching with all state vars reset confirmed — all 7 vars (activeTab, filterCategory, filterProject, filterQuery, editingId, confirmDeleteId, movingId) cleared on tab change.

KNOWN ISSUE (UX, not a FAIL): Edit form submit catch block uses inline msgEl.innerHTML injection instead of showError(app, ...). This intentionally preserves the form state so the user does not lose their edits on a save failure. The four destructive-action catch blocks (load, delete, promote, move) all correctly call showError(app, ...). Flagged as low-priority improvement, not an AC violation given the deliberate design intent.

comments.note: views/knowledge.js (line 480–482): Edit form catch block uses inline msgEl.innerHTML injection rather than showError(app, ...). This is a deliberate UX decision — preserving form state on save failure — but is inconsistent with AC-11's 'via showError(app, ...)' wording. 4 of 5 error paths use showError(app, ...) correctly. Recommend the Reviewer assess whether this should be aligned or explicitly documented as an exception.

views/knowledge.js: The WP deliverables spec lists state variables as allInsights, activeTab, filterCategory, filterProject, filterQuery, editingId, confirmDeleteId — omitting movingId. The implementation correctly adds movingId (required for the Move to Project feature). Tab switching also resets movingId. No functional issue, but the spec was slightly incomplete.

views/knowledge.js (formatConfidence): Values like 0.6799 round to 68% (High) due to Math.round(67.99) = 68. This means the effective Medium-to-High boundary is slightly below 0.68, not exactly 0.68. This is inherent to floating-point rounding and is acceptable for a UX confidence display, but could confuse users who see a card marked 'High' at 67.99%. Not a bug, but worth noting in code comments.

views/knowledge.js: renderList() rebuilds the filter bar DOM on every keystroke, causing the search input to lose focus. This was flagged by the Developer in implementation comments. Confirmed during static analysis — wireFilterBarEvents() is called on every renderList() invocation. Workaround: cache filterQuery before rebuild and refocus after. This is a known UX degradation and was acknowledged as functional but suboptimal.

summary: Reviewed mcp-server/gui/public/views/knowledge.js against all four review dimensions (maintainability, best practices, performance, future context). All 11 ACs confirmed met. No blocking issues found.

Fix-Forward (1): Removed dead `if (action === 'save-edit')` branch in the event delegation handler. The Save button uses type=submit and is handled by the form's submit listener — the data-action branch was unreachable and misleading.

Fix-Forward (2): Added an explicit inline comment to the edit form's catch block documenting the intentional deviation from showError(app,...). The inline msgEl error approach correctly preserves form state on save failure; the comment makes this design decision visible to future maintainers.

QA sign-off on AC-11 exception: The edit form catch block using msgEl.innerHTML instead of showError(app,...) is a deliberate, well-reasoned UX choice. All four destructive-action paths (load, delete, promote, move) use showError(app,...) correctly. The exception is now documented in-code.

Architecture is sound: event delegation pattern is consistent with other views, all user input is escapeHtml'd before interpolation, state management is simple and correct, no polling registered, formatConfidence constants are named and correct.
Known UX degradation (filter-bar rebuild on keystroke causing focus loss) acknowledged as a follow-up improvement, not a blocker for this WP.

comments.note: Removed dead `if (action === 'save-edit') { return; }` branch from the event delegation click handler (wireEvents). The Save button is type=submit and handled exclusively by the form's submit listener — the data-action='save-edit' path was never reachable and falsely implied a second code path existed. Non-behavioral change.

Added explanatory comment to the edit form's .catch() block documenting why msgEl.innerHTML is used instead of showError(app,...). The comment reads: 'Intentional: inline error preserves form state so the user does not lose edits on a transient save failure. All destructive actions (delete/promote/move) use showError(app,...) because they navigate away or remove the card.' This makes the AC-11 exception explicit and self-documenting for future maintainers. Non-behavioral change.

renderList() accepts `categories` and `projects` parameters but wireFilterBarEvents() (called internally) re-collects these values independently from allInsights, making the parameters redundant pass-throughs. At < 1,000 entries this is harmless, but the signature is slightly misleading. A future cleanup could either remove the params (have wireFilterBarEvents() always derive from allInsights) or pass them through consistently.

renderList() rebuilds the entire filter bar DOM on every keystroke (confirmed). The search input loses focus on each keypress. The fix is minimal and non-behavioral: after filter bar rebuild, re-query the input and call .focus(). Consider applying in a follow-up WP or during the wiring WP (WP-008).

[documentation-forward] views/knowledge.js: Document the intentional AC-11 exception for the edit form error path — the inline msgEl error display is a deliberate UX choice (preserves form state on save failure) distinct from showError(app,...) used by destructive actions. A code comment explains this, but the README or developer notes should also mention that this pattern diverges from the general error-display convention.

[documentation-forward] views/knowledge.js: The movingId state variable is required for the Move to Project feature but is absent from the WP deliverables spec. The spec should be updated (or a note added) to list movingId alongside the other state variables so future developers have an accurate reference.

[documentation-forward] views/knowledge.js formatConfidence(): A code comment should note that Math.round() means values like 0.6799 display as 68% (High), making the effective Medium→High boundary slightly below the 0.68 constant. This is correct UX behaviour but could confuse future maintainers adjusting the thresholds.
